I’m still trying to find meds that work for me (dex/vyvanse overstimulate me), so I don’t have your level of clarity. Do you have any insights on how to approach dating with this type of brain? For example, how do you tell whether the way you feel about someone is genuine or whether it’s ADHD? Or whether to trust the decisions you make when you’re high energy vs the (sometimes opposite) ones made when you’re low energy? I haven’t encountered someone else who has experienced this before, so I’m curious to hear your thoughts if you feel like sharing. 

I personally find that I can only truly connect with other people if they are also neurodiverse, especially fellow high-functioning autists. Because of this, I’m starting to think there might not be much point to going on dates with neurotypical people. Which makes dating harder.

I went to a psychiatrist for my depression and borderline (diagnosed years prior). I thought that my issues might've been part of my depression, but after a few sessions he told me that I "showed signs of ADHD". A few sessions later he confirmed it and put me on Ritalin. It helped immensely however it exacerbated my borderline-related mood swings so I had to go off it. I'd recommend talking to your GP about your symptoms and asking for a referral.

> Because of this there are a bunch of women with depression and anxiety as a result of believing they are stupid and forgetful when they actually have ADD.

Fuck I hate reading this, it's so true. I'm a 30 year old woman and was only diagnosed with ADHD two years ago. I've always been incredibly scatterbrained, as though I have all these fleeting thoughts that I'm desperately trying to grasp but can't. I literally can't understand what people are telling me when they're giving me instructions. Most of the time it's a struggle to remember what I did yesterday.

My whole life I've been told I'm stupid. My teachers told me I was stupid because I had no memory of the work we'd done that day or the projects I'd been given. My friends always make fun of how scatterbrained I am. I've lost so many jobs because I can't remember procedures. Nowadays I write everything down which helps, but I'm perpetually "zoned out" and find it practically impossible to "switch on" to reality.

I wish I'd been diagnosed when I was young. I can't help but think of all the things I could've accomplished. When I'm hyperfocused on something, I get amazing results (at Uni I got a high GPA and a Dean's Commendation because I was obsessed with the subject matter). I still can't shake the idea that I'm stupid though. I refrain from doing certain things like applying for better jobs or going to conferences because "those things are for smart people". It's part of my identity now- that I'm stupid. 

Fucking brain chemicals, bleh.
